newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki seen starting higher, but less vigorous.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki seen starting higher, but less vigorous.

text.p: Shares were seen opening higher on Wednesday after U.S. stocks surged overnight, but brokers said the rise would be less vigorous than the 2.5 percent climb on the HEX index on Tuesday.
"We'll go higher today, but it won't be anything near as spectacular as yesterday," one broker said, predicting the HEX index would rise less than one percent for the day.
Nokia was expected to be in focus again on Wednesday after it held most of its Helsinki gains on Wall Street overnight, closing in New York at about 321.00 markka.
Brokers said they would also be eyeing Rautaruukki, which ended up sharply at 46.50 on Tuesday, above its share offering price of 42.00 markka per share.
Financial shares could draw strength from the bullish bond market and lower interest rates, brokers said.
But trading could be subdued ahead of the May 1 holiday, they said.
